driver: STM32N6 independent watchdog (IWDG) HAL driver (on the verified IWDG LL driver)

source_documents: RM0486 Rev 4 chapter 59 (IWDG) + memory map p.179
target.hsi_contract: RM0486 Rev 4 ch.59 IWDG register interface + memory map p.179 (IWDG secure base 0x56004800)
target.safety_allocation: NOT_PROVIDED: no owner safety scope recorded for the IWDG work orders

scope: HAL: hal_status_t API with HAL_IWDG_ prefix, a const configuration pointer, parameter checks and a timeout-bounded wait, built only on the PROVIDED LL_IWDG_ functions

Initialise the watchdog (RM0486 59.3, window option disabled): start key, register access key, prescaler (IWDG_PR.PR) and reload (IWDG_RLR.RL), wait until the update flags IWDG_SR.PVU and IWDG_SR.RVU are cleared - the wait bounded in TIME by a caller-supplied timeout in milliseconds of the system time base HAL_GetTick() (at most 48 ms, covering the RM0486 update time of up to 6 LSI periods), never by a count of polling iterations - then refresh the counter
On an update timeout: write-protect IWDG_PR/IWDG_RLR again (a key other than 0x5555), do not refresh, and return HAL_TIMEOUT; the started watchdog keeps running (it cannot be stopped)
The LL header is provided read-only (verified IWDG LL work order) and is not modified
Out of scope: window option (IWDG_WINR), early wake-up interrupt (IWDG_EWCR, IWDG_ICR), hardware watchdog option bytes, low-power freeze, debug freeze; stopping the watchdog (impossible once started)
